hints: To move n disks, first move the top n-1 disks to the spare peg.
Move the largest disk directly to the destination.
Move the n-1 disks from the spare peg onto the largest disk; recurse using the appropriate peg labels.
analogy: The largest disk is blocked until every smaller disk is moved away, then the same smaller-disk task repeats.
example: With two disks: move disk 1 from peg 1 to 2, disk 2 from 1 to 3, then disk 1 from 2 to 3: three moves.
algorithm: Use recursive Hanoi(n, from, spare, to): solve Hanoi(n-1, from, to, spare), emit from-to, then solve Hanoi(n-1, spare, from, to). Print 2^n-1 before listing moves.
correctness: The largest disk must move exactly once after all smaller disks leave it; the two recursive transfers are necessary and optimal by induction.
complexity: O(2^n) time and output space, with O(n) recursion depth.
